title: Answer your three most common replies
outcomes: Reads the three most common replies to his own line from the Openings page data and names the reason for each answer
Finds a sound move in unlabeled positions after each common reply
Tells which common replies have many good answers and which have few
Leaves rare replies unprepared on purpose

steps.text: In **Start a small repertoire from the games you actually face** you listed the lines you meet. Now answer the *replies*. After 1.d4 d5 2.c4 on the Openings page (band 1100-1300, 18,156 games), Black plays ...dxc4 in 38% (6,927), ...e6 in 18% (3,244) and ...Nf6 in 17% (3,063). That is 73% in three replies. ...c6 follows with 13%. Study one answer, then try two.

steps.caption: After 2...e6: develop, then decide the centre later.

line.say: A knight develops and watches d5 and e4.
The bishop pins the knight to the queen.
Black unpins by developing the bishop.
The pawn opens the f1 bishop.

claims.statement: 3.Nc3, 3.Nf3, 3.cxd5, 3.e3 and 3.Qc2 are each within 40 centipawns of the engine's first choice (depth 16).

steps.text: **What the numbers say.** After ...dxc4 and ...e6 many moves work, so write a reason (develop, retake the pawn later) instead of memorising a move. After ...Nf6 fewer moves work. **Rule of thumb:** keep memory for positions where one slip loses; where several moves work, write the reason. Next: many good moves, few, and a rare reply.

steps.title: Many good moves, few, or a rare reply
steps.prompt: White to move in each position. Predict how many moves work, then check.
Do the same for your own first move. Use the Openings page at your rating, or tally your own games once you have about twenty (small tallies are noisy [H]).
